investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-17T20:34–20:41Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, so the eval runner could not reach the agent creation or readiness steps required by the expected-output contract.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place any remote-agent pod on the 6-node production cluster. Two nodes expose the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource but reported Insufficient capacity at the time of each probe run; the other four nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector. Preemption was also unavailable on both resource-carrying nodes. Because the pod never became Running, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) timed out after ~144 s without writing any evidence, causing all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) to remain missing and the contract assertion (vmIdPresent=true, remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready]) to go unevaluated. This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Most likely — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both capable nodes: all concurrent or recently-created remote-agent pods have consumed the available VM slots on the 2 nodes that carry this resource, leaving zero allocatable capacity for new pods at the time of the probe runs.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector, possibly because a label was removed, a node was cordoned, or the pod spec's affinity rules were tightened and no longer match the current node topology.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning for kata.peerpods.io/vm workloads: the total kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity across the cluster (limited to 2 nodes) is insufficient to absorb concurrent probe and production workloads simultaneously, causing transient exhaustion during peak scheduling windows.

Lower confidence — node-level issue on the 2 kata-capable nodes: one or both nodes may be under memory/CPU pressure, in a NotReady state, or have the kata.peerpods.io/vm device plugin reporting reduced capacity, causing the scheduler to see Insufficient resources even if slots appear available in the node spec.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-17T20:36–20:41Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the requested pod because 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent was never created, and the eval runner could not collect any of the required evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state), causing a complete contract gap.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler reported "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" for every remote-agent pod creation attempt. The kata.peerpods.io/vm resource is a finite, node-advertised extended resource used to gate peer-pod (confidential VM) scheduling. With only 2 nodes eligible by affinity and both exhausted of that resource, no pod could be placed. Preemption was also unavailable ("No preemption victims found"). The eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) therefore never returned a live agent, so the probe terminated early and produced an empty evidence object, violating all four required evidence fields in the contract defined at check-expectations.json line 264.

With only 2 nodes eligible by affinity and both exhausted of that resource, no pod could be placed. Preemption was also unavailable ("No preemption victims found"). The eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) therefore never returned a live agent, so the probe terminated early and produced an empty evidence object, violating all four required evidence fields in the contract defined at check-expectations.json line 264.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Kata/PeerPods VM Capacity Exhausted — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Unschedulable
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-07-17T20:36–20:41Z with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages reporting that 0 of 6 nodes could schedule the probe pod: 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never scheduled, no agent was created, and the runtime eval produced zero evidence — every required field (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) is missing. This is an eval-infrastructure failure caused by exhausted or misconfigured Kata PeerPods VM capacity in the production-api Kubernetes cluster; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent probe pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources, meaning the PeerPods VM quota on those nodes was fully consumed at the time of each eval run. The remaining 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector at all. Preemption was also unavailable on both eligible nodes (no lower-priority victims found). As a result, the pod remained Unschedulable for ~142–144 seconds across all three checks before the eval timed out, and no agent was ever provisioned. The complete absence of evidence (failed-check.evidence is empty; all 5 required evidence keys are missing) is a direct consequence of the scheduling failure, not a contract or runner code defect.

[Likely] Sustained or concurrent load on the PeerPods-capable nodes: if other remote-agent workloads or prior eval runs did not fully release their VM slots before this run, the quota would appear exhausted even if total capacity is nominally sufficient.

[Possible] Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector at all, meaning only 2 nodes are even eligible. [Lower likelihood] Transient scheduler state: a brief resource spike that resolved after the eval timeout; would be disproved if subsequent runs pass without intervention.
